title: Observability
tagline: Make a wrong answer explain itself without leaking the data behind it.
story: The answer was wrong and nobody can say why. A classic service fails with an error, but an LLM system returns a fluent 200 that happens to be false, spread across model calls, tools and several agents. This world teaches you to record enough to explain a run, keep customer text out of the places it should not be, and meter cost and quality without drowning in data.
oneLiner: Record the shape of every run by default, keep content behind an explicit policy, and alert on metrics because metrics are not sampled.
youWillLearn: Explain why LLM observability differs from classic service monitoring, and which signals matter
Name the OpenTelemetry GenAI spans and attributes (chat, invoke_agent, execute_tool, invoke_workflow) and read their Development status honestly
Choose a content capture policy by sensitivity, debugging need, access control and effort, and know which flag controls which layer
Carry trace context across HTTP, MCP `params._meta` and A2A, and spot where hosted MCP tools break the chain
Sample traces without distorting totals, and count tokens with counters instead of sampled spans
Pick SLIs, SLOs and a backend (Foundry with Application Insights, Aspire, Langfuse, LangSmith, Phoenix) for your constraints
Defend a debuggable and private multi-agent design

flashcards.front: Why is a green trace not proof of a good answer?
flashcards.back: A wrong answer is a fluent success: HTTP 200 and no `error.type`. You need finish reasons, tool calls, token counts and quality scores on the run to see semantic failures.

flashcards.front: What is the status of the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions on 2026-10-13?
flashcards.back: Development, not stable. They moved to `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai` on 2026-05-05. That repo has no tagged release, so pin by commit.

flashcards.front: Name the span name patterns for a model call, an agent run and a workflow run.
flashcards.back: `{gen_ai.operation.name} {gen_ai.request.model}`, `invoke_agent {gen_ai.agent.name}` and `invoke_workflow {gen_ai.workflow.name}`. Agent Framework names its tool spans `execute_tool <function_name>`.

flashcards.front: Which attributes are required on a GenAI inference span?
flashcards.back: `gen_ai.operation.name` and `gen_ai.provider.name`. Common extras include `error.type`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` and the `gen_ai.usage.*` token attributes.

flashcards.front: What does the spec say about recording prompts and outputs by default?
flashcards.back: Instrumentations SHOULD NOT capture them by default. Content attributes are opt-in: `gen_ai.input.messages`, `gen_ai.output.messages`, `gen_ai.system_instructions`, `gen_ai.tool.definitions`, `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` and `gen_ai.tool.call.result`.

flashcards.front: What are the three content capture patterns in the spec?
flashcards.back: Record nothing (default). Record content on spans, suited to pre-production or telemetry that meets privacy rules. Store content externally and put references on spans, recommended for production.

flashcards.front: Which layer does each content flag control?
flashcards.back: `ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA` (default false) is the Agent Framework flag. `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT` is the OTel and Azure SDK flag. `AZURE_TRACING_GEN_AI_CONTENT_RECORDING_ENABLED` is the older Foundry classic one.

flashcards.front: What does `@trace_function` do regardless of the content flag?
flashcards.back: It always records parameters and return values, so it can leak data even when content capture is off.

flashcards.front: How does trace context cross an MCP call?
flashcards.back: The client injects W3C `traceparent`, `tracestate` and `baggage` into `params._meta` of the request, with unprefixed keys. The server extracts them as the remote parent. MCP revision 2026-07-28 reserves those keys.

flashcards.front: Which MCP tools break trace propagation in Agent Framework Python?
flashcards.back: Hosted or provider-managed tools such as `get_mcp_tool(...)` on Foundry, OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini clients and Foundry toolboxes, because the provider runtime makes the call. Client-opened transports do get `params._meta`.

flashcards.front: What is the shape of a `traceparent` header?
flashcards.back: `00-<32 hex trace id>-<16 hex parent id>-<2 hex flags>`. W3C Trace Context Level 1 is a Recommendation (2021-11-23). Level 2 is a Candidate Recommendation Draft (2024-03-28).

flashcards.front: Why alert on metrics and not on traces?
flashcards.back: Metrics are not sampled in Application Insights, so rates and counts stay exact. Traces are sampled, and the Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro defaults to rate-limited sampling at five traces per second.

Head decides at the start of a trace, cheaply, so it cannot keep every error trace. Tail decides after the whole trace is seen, so it can keep errors and slow traces, at the cost of compute and engineering effort.

flashcards.front: Token usage counters versus per-operation histograms?
flashcards.back: Counters (`gen_ai.client.inference.usage.*`) are for totals and cost. The per-operation histograms are for percentiles and outliers and should not be used for total usage or cost.

flashcards.front: Are cached and reasoning tokens extra tokens?
flashcards.back: No. Cached tokens are a subset of input tokens and reasoning tokens are a subset of output tokens. Adding them on top double counts.

flashcards.front: Which limits bite when you attribute token cost at an API gateway?
flashcards.back: APIM `llm-emit-token-metric`: up to five custom dimensions, 100 unique values per dimension and 1,000 active time series per namespace, with the excess dropped silently. Azure Monitor allows 10 dimension keys per metric.

flashcards.front: Why can Langfuse show nothing from a default Agent Framework Python exporter?
flashcards.back: The Python default is OTLP over gRPC, and Langfuse accepts OTLP over HTTP (JSON or protobuf) only. Set an HTTP protocol. This follows from the two pages, not from a vendor statement.

flashcards.front: Which SLIs suit an agent run?
flashcards.back: Run availability, p95 run duration excluding human pauses, p95 time to first chunk, tool error ratio, p99 model and tool calls per run, tokens per successful task and the online evaluation pass rate. They are design suggestions, not vendor numbers.

glossary.def: Shared names for spans, attributes and metrics of model, agent, tool and MCP calls. All carry status Development as of 2026-10-13 and live in `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai`.
One timed operation inside a trace, with a name, kind, attributes and a parent. A run becomes a tree of spans.
The span for one agent run, named `invoke_agent {gen_ai.agent.name}`. Its children are the model calls and tool calls of that run.
The operation name for running a tool. Agent Framework names the span `execute_tool <function_name>`.
The W3C header `00-<trace id>-<parent id>-<flags>` that carries a trace across a hop. MCP carries it in `params._meta` and HTTP carries it as a header.
Key-value context that travels with a trace across hops. MCP reserves `baggage` in `_meta` next to `traceparent` and `tracestate`.
Recording prompts, outputs, tool arguments and tool results on spans. Off by default in the spec and in Agent Framework (`ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA`).
Deciding whether to keep a trace when it starts, for example a fixed ratio of 5 percent. Cheap, but it cannot keep every error trace.
Deciding whether to keep a trace after all its spans are seen, so errors and slow traces can be kept. It costs compute and engineering effort.
A measured ratio or percentile of good behaviour, such as the share of agent runs without `error.type`.
A target for an SLI over a window, chosen from your own baseline. Burn alerts fire when the error budget is being spent too fast.
The OpenTelemetry wire protocol, over gRPC or HTTP. Agent Framework Python defaults to gRPC, and Langfuse accepts only HTTP.
The Azure Monitor store for traces, metrics and logs. Foundry tracing writes to it, and its sampling and `itemCount` fields affect how you count.
A cumulative token metric such as `gen_ai.client.inference.usage.input_tokens`. Use it for totals and cost, because it is not sampled the way traces are.

claims.text: All GenAI semantic conventions carry status Development and moved to open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai (PR 3696 merged 2026-05-05); the new repo has no tags or releases.
v1.41.1 (2026-05-11) of the old repo still holds the full GenAI docs and v1.42.0 (2026-06-12) holds only a Moved stub.
Inference spans are named {gen_ai.operation.name} {gen_ai.request.model}, kind CLIENT; gen_ai.operation.name and gen_ai.provider.name are required.
Agent spans are named invoke_agent {gen_ai.agent.name}: CLIENT for remote agent services and INTERNAL for in-process frameworks; invoke_workflow {gen_ai.workflow.name} is INTERNAL.

Agent Framework emits spans invoke_agent <agent_name>, chat <model_name> and execute_tool <function_name>, and metrics gen_ai.client.operation.duration, gen_ai.client.token.usage and agent_framework.function.invocation.duration.

Agent Framework workflow spans include workflow.build, workflow.run (Python) or workflow.session (.NET and Go), executor.process {executor_id}, edge_group.process and message.send; executor.input, executor.output and message.content appear only when sensitive data is on.
The v1.41 docs defined a gen_ai.client.token.usage histogram; the new repo defines usage counters gen_ai.client.inference.usage.* while Agent Framework docs still list the older name.
In .NET, gen_ai.* spans appear only after the client or agent is wrapped with UseOpenTelemetry; the Harness wraps both by default.

Instrumentations SHOULD NOT capture content by default; the opt-in attributes are gen_ai.system_instructions, gen_ai.input.messages, gen_ai.output.messages, gen_ai.tool.definitions, gen_ai.tool.call.arguments and gen_ai.tool.call.result.

The spec names three usage patterns: record nothing, record content on spans for pre-production or privacy-compliant telemetry, and store content externally with references on spans, recommended for production.
An in-process upload hook runs regardless of the span sampling decision and independent of the opt-in flags.

Agent Framework ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA defaults to false and covers prompts, responses, tool arguments and tool results; Python instrumentation has been on by default since python-1.6.0 (2026-05-21) with no exporter installed automatically.
In .NET, instrumenting both the chat client and the agent duplicates prompts and responses on both spans when sensitive data is on.

The @trace_function decorator always records parameters and return values regardless of the content recording flag; the content flag is OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT, replacing the older AZURE_TRACING_GEN_AI_CONTENT_RECORDING_ENABLED.
MCP trace context travels as W3C traceparent, tracestate and baggage in params._meta with unprefixed keys, and the MCP span is named {mcp.method.name} {target}.
MCP revision 2026-07-28 reserves traceparent, tracestate and baggage in _meta as an exception to the vendor-prefix rule.

Agent Framework Python injects trace context into params._meta only for MCP sessions it opens itself (MCPStreamableHTTPTool, MCPStdioTool, MCPWebsocketTool), not for hosted or provider-managed MCP tools.

traceparent has the shape 00-<32 hex trace id>-<16 hex parent id>-<2 hex flags>; W3C Trace Context Level 1 is a Recommendation (2021-11-23) and Level 2 is a Candidate Recommendation Draft (2024-03-28).
A2A guidance says clients and servers should participate in distributed tracing with W3C Trace Context over HTTP; the spec defines no tracing fields.
The Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro defaults to rate-limited sampling at five traces per second; fixed ratio is the alternative and 5 percent (0.05) is the suggested start; metrics are not sampled.
Head sampling decides early and cannot guarantee every error trace is kept; tail sampling decides on the whole trace but costs compute and engineering effort.
Usage counter input_tokens includes cached tokens and output_tokens includes reasoning tokens; per-operation histograms should not be used for total usage or cost.

APIM llm-emit-token-metric allows up to five custom dimensions, 100 unique values per dimension and 1,000 active time series per namespace and drops the excess silently; Azure Monitor allows 10 dimension keys per metric.
Langfuse receives OTLP at /api/public/otel over HTTP JSON or HTTP protobuf and does not support gRPC.
LangSmith takes OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://api.smith.langchain.com/otel with an x-api-key header, and the base endpoint must not include /v1/traces.
Foundry server-side tracing is GA for prompt and hosted agents, client-side tracing is preview, and the portal Traces tab shows 90 days.
The Application Insights Agents view is preview, shows agent runs, tool calls, models and errors, sorts traces by tokens used and comes with prebuilt Grafana dashboards.
The standalone Aspire Dashboard takes OTLP on port 4317 and serves its UI on port 18888 in the Agent Framework local setup.
